Very fun 2D arcade style plane shooter. It reminds me a little of the 1942/1943 arcade games, but instead of the classic static format where you can only move your plane from side to side, it's full 360 degree movement. There are dozens of unlockable customisation parts that not only change your planes weapons, armour and movement, they also change the soundtrack of the game. Unlike most plane shooters, there are no bosses (not that I've encountered), but there are different enemy types such as fighter planes, jets, boats, airships etc.

There is no health bar either. Instead, your plane will display various amounts of damage, and a circle around the plane will shrink smaller and smaller as you get hit more. Whereas similar games have health pickups, in Luftrausers you just stop shooting and your plane will heal itself, which adds a sort of strategy to the game because sometimes it's better to shoot a plane down that's shooting at you, and sometimes it's better to fly away.

It is extremely fast paced, but not impossible due to your plane being extremely easy to maneuver. The visuals are sepia coloured, which looks a little bland upon first glance but the simplicity is actually pretty nice. The only bad thing about it is it's a bit difficult to see the water when you first start playing, but you get used to it. There is an option to change the game skin/colours, so I think you can unlock them, but I'm not entirely sure as I haven't got that far yet.

It is $10 on Steam.

Arcady, very early on, showed a huge fascination with all kinds of adventure stories. The traditional heroes and their bold undertakings to rescue a damsel in distress. Soon enough she started to think about becoming an author herself. "Someday, when I'm grown up!" She used to say. On her 12th birthday morning, her father decided to take her out into the field. Arcady had no idea what her father had in mind, but she saw him smile and his eyes shine bright like a star. "A place that always made me imagine my own adventures!", he said. "Something inspirational!" Arcady could not resist, smiled at her dad and made herself ready for the trip. A quick breakfast and some words Arcady will never forget, when her dad said, "Time to write your own stories, darling!".
